text: In nine months, Intel went from left-for-dead — to the comeback story of the decade.
Last August, Intel hit nineteen dollars. Q2 losses: two-point-nine billion.
CEO Lip-Bu Tan cut fifteen percent of the staff.
Then August 22nd — the US government bought ten percent of Intel. At twenty-dollars-forty-seven a share.
SoftBank: two billion. Nvidia: five billion — and they're building chips with Intel.
Tan killed Europe's fabs. Slowed Ohio. No more blank checks.
Q1 twenty-twenty-six — Intel beat revenue by one-point-two billion. The sixth straight beat.
Data center revenue up twenty-two percent. Nvidia, Google — running on Intel's Xeon 6.
Last week — Apple, in talks to make chips at Intel. The stock hit an all-time high.
